issues.description: The last-active-Owner lockout protection added for member suspend/remove is enforced only in the Next.js API route layer (organization-members PATCH/DELETE) and is missing entirely from the DB/RLS layer that governs kontrolia_auth.membership_roles — an org Admin can DELETE the sole Owner's role-assignment row directly via PostgREST/Supabase and strip Owner authority with no last-owner check at all.
evidence: packages/db/migrations/0010_rls_policies.sql:78-81 — "org admins manage membership roles" policy is a bare is_org_admin() check with no last-owner guard
packages/db/migrations/0009_helper_functions.sql:19-36 — is_org_admin() returns true for slug 'owner' OR 'admin', so a non-Owner Admin passes this policy

apps/auth-server/app/api/organization-members/route.ts:107-144 — wouldRemoveLastOwner() exists and is called from PATCH (line 165) and DELETE (line 198) on memberships only, never referenced from any membership_roles code path
packages/db/migrations/0013_audit_log_triggers.sql:89-116 — role.unassigned audit trigger confirms DELETE on membership_roles is an expected, reachable, normal operation, not a theoretical edge case
verification: Read the RLS policy text directly and confirmed no last-owner-count subquery or trigger exists anywhere in the migrations for membership_roles

Confirmed the admin-panel UI itself only ever edits app-scoped roles (apps/admin-panel/app/users/page.tsx:139-165 filters .not("application_id","is",null)) so the gap is only reachable via a direct authenticated API call, not through the shipped UI — still a real gap since the endpoint itself has no server-side guard

history.note: Same bug class as the plan-compliance CRITICAL fixed today in commit 4579870 (suspend-to-zero-active-Owners lockout) but through a different, DB-level door that fix never covered. An Admin (not just an Owner) can strip the sole Owner's org-wide role and reproduce the exact lockout scenario the earlier fix was meant to close.

issues.description: The platform-admins DELETE (revoke) route's "don't remove the last platform admin" check is a plain SELECT COUNT(*) followed by a separate DELETE, not an atomic check — two concurrent revoke requests when count===2 can both read count=2, both pass the <=1 guard, and both succeed, leaving zero platform admins.
evidence: apps/auth-server/app/api/platform-admins/route.ts:110-120 — COUNT then DELETE as two separate, non-atomic statements
verification: Read the DELETE handler in full and confirmed the count-check and the delete are two separate round-trips with no transaction/row-lock between them

history.note: Low likelihood (requires two admins concurrently revoking down to the same last-two boundary) but the outcome — zero platform admins, no recovery path except direct DB access — is severe, and it's the exact same TOCTOU pattern the org-owner fix was meant to close, just not propagated here.
